description: This topic covers the study of electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic fields. Understanding these principles is crucial for the General Science section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Static Electricity and Charges
sections.description: Study of electric charges and their behavior in a static state.

key_concepts.explanation: The fundamental property of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electromagnetic field. Its SI unit is the Coulomb (C).
Materials that contain a high number of free electrons, allowing electric current to flow through them easily (e.g., Silver, Copper).
Materials that resist the flow of electric charge because they have negligible free electrons (e.g., Rubber, Glass, Wood).

scientific_principles.application: Used to calculate the electrostatic force of attraction or repulsion between two point charges.
Represents the force experienced by a unit positive charge placed at a specific point in an electric field.

sections.title: Electric Current and Circuits
sections.description: Analysis of moving charges and the core components of electrical circuits.

key_concepts.explanation: The rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor. Its SI unit is the Ampere (A).
The amount of work done in moving a unit charge from one point to another in an electric circuit. Its SI unit is the Volt (V).
The property of a conductor to resist the flow of electric current through it. Its SI unit is the Ohm (Ω).

scientific_principles.application: States that at a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends.
Used to increase the total resistance in an electrical circuit.
Used to decrease the total resistance in an electrical circuit, commonly used in domestic household wiring.

key_associations.extra_info: Always connected in series in a circuit; an ideal ammeter has zero resistance.
Always connected in parallel in a circuit; an ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance.

sections.title: Magnetism and Magnetic Fields
sections.description: Introduction to the properties of magnets and the magnetic fields they generate.

key_concepts.explanation: The region around a magnet where its magnetic influence or force can be detected. Its SI unit is the Tesla (T).
Imaginary continuous closed curves that emerge from the North Pole and merge at the South Pole outside the magnet.

important_facts.fact: Like magnetic poles always repel each other, whereas unlike poles attract each other.
A freely suspended bar magnet always aligns itself in the geographic North-South direction.
Two magnetic field lines never intersect each other.

sections.title: Electromagnetic Induction
sections.description: The relationship between electricity and magnetism and their practical applications.

key_concepts.explanation: The phenomenon of generating an induced electromotive force (EMF) and current in a closed circuit by changing the magnetic field linked with it.
An electric current that reverses its direction periodically at regular time intervals.
An electric current that flows consistently in only one direction.

scientific_principles.application: The magnitude of the induced EMF is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Thumb = Force/Motion, Index Finger = Magnetic Field, Middle Finger = Current
scientific_principles.application: Used to find the direction of the force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field (applied in Electric Motors).

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Thumb = Motion of Conductor, Index Finger = Magnetic Field, Middle Finger = Induced Current
scientific_principles.application: Used to find the direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field (applied in Electric Generators).

key_associations.associated_with: Converts Electrical Energy into Mechanical Energy
key_associations.extra_info: Works on the principle of the magnetic effect of electric current.

key_associations.associated_with: Converts Mechanical Energy into Electrical Energy
key_associations.extra_info: Works on the principle of electromagnetic induction.

key_associations.associated_with: Steps up or Steps down AC Voltage
key_associations.extra_info: Works on the principle of mutual induction and operates only on Alternating Current (AC), not DC.
